newsitem.title: USA: White House says Rangel tax plan "positive effort".
newsitem.headline: White House says Rangel tax plan "positive effort".

text.p: The White House praised a tax proposal by Rep. Charles Rangel, a New York Democrat, as a "very positive effort" and a plausible alternative to a tax program unveiled by a top Republican legislator on Monday.

"The more Gene Sperling and the economic council guys look at the details of Congressman Rangel's bill, the more they are satisfied that that represents a lot of effort to incorporate the president's proposals, particularly with respect to education," White House spokesman Mike McCurry told reporters.
Sperling is the chairman of the National Economic Council, the main economic policy-making body within the White House.
"There is much to like in the Rangel bill and not a great deal of difference to some of the approaches that we have," he added. "By and large, we think it's a very positive effort."

Clinton and his top advisers have sharply criticized a five-year, $85 billion tax cut plan drafted by Rep. Bill Archer, the Texas Republican who chairs the House Ways and Means Committee, which writes tax legislation.
Clinton Tuesday said Archer's bill violates the balanced budget agreement reached between Clinton and Republicans.
McCurry called the Rangel proposal "a far preferable starting point than what the chairman came up with."
